lines.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night crew is outside saying they are filming an observation camera for the Best Friends Special today.
What—without prior permission?! Why did nobody warn me in advance when I do not even have proper makeup on?!
And of all people, that umbrella rookie producer came—CEO Byun dislikes him too, so why do they keep pairing him with you?
Wait, who came?! Tell him to leave this instant!
If you want me inside I will stay, or outside I will step out—what do you want, should I wedge myself in the doorway?

lines.trans: Go right ahead if you want!

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!
Did you hear about this personally?
I was busy today because of personally.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

examples.text: 우리 공과 사는 구분하죠. 이건 공적인 스케줄이니까 사적인 대화는 삼가는 게 좋겠다는 얘기예요.
examples.trans: Let us draw a line between public work and private life—since this is an official shoot, let us refrain from private talk.
This point about official, public is really important.

examples.text: 밖에 1박 팀에서 오늘 절친 특집 관찰 카메라 한다고 찾아왔어.
examples.trans: The 2 Days & 1 Night crew is outside saying they are filming an observation camera for the Best Friends Special today.
This point about observation is really important.
How do you tell whether someone has a kid's palate?
This expression comes from 'can one tell apart?'.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

examples.text: 야, 근데 거기 내가 왜 끼냐고?
examples.trans: Hey, why on earth would I get dragged into that?
This expression comes from 'get roped in?'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

나가다.gloss: to go out, to step outside

meanings.en: to go out, to step outside, to leave a room

examples.trans: Let's step outside for a moment and talk.
He went out of the conference room.

meanings.note: interrogative pronoun; becomes 누가 before subject particle -가

examples.trans: Did someone come outside?
Who is that person?
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.en: immediately, on the spot, right this second
meanings.note: often paired with 지금 (지금 당장) for strong emphasis

examples.trans: Try calling right away.
We have to start right this second.
He is our company's president.
I will speak as the representative.

examples.text: 아니요 저는 아무도 아닙니다, 대화 편하게 나누세요. 저는 진짜 수상한 사람인 줄 알고…
examples.trans: Oh no, I am nobody special—please chat comfortably. I genuinely thought he was a suspicious person…
This point about conversation is really important.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.
The manager called.
Where is Cindy's manager?

examples.text: 메이크업이 좀 센 거 같지 않아요? 좀 러블리하고 귀엽고 착해 보이고 그런 거.
examples.trans: Does my makeup not look a bit too fierce? Make it softer—more lovely, cute, and sweet-looking.
Here the word for 'makeup' is key.

문틈.gloss: in the crack of the door

meanings.en: in the crack of the door

examples.text: 여기 있으라면 있고 나가 있으라면 나가 있을게. 어떻게, 나 문틈에 껴 있을까?
examples.trans: If you want me inside I will stay, or outside I will step out—what do you want, should I wedge myself in the doorway?
This point about in the crack of the door is really important.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

examples.text: 제가 이번 주에는 꼭 의상 미리 보겠습니다.
examples.trans: This week I will definitely check the stage outfit in advance.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?
It rains outside.
Fell out of favor.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

examples.text: 사람들이 연예인 이름 앞에 별명을 붙였는데 웃기더라고.
examples.trans: People put nicknames in front of celebrities' names, and it was really funny.

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 붙이다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (attached, added).

meanings.note: Sino-Korean suffix/syllable found in prestigious professions like 의사 ('doctor') and 판사 ('judge')

examples.trans: Both 'doctor' and 'lawyer' end in the syllable 'sa'.
Father likes professions that include the syllable 'sa'.

examples.text: 선수들끼리 사적인 감정은 감정, 일은 일인데!
examples.trans: Between pros like us, personal feelings are personal feelings and business is business!
Here the word for 'personal' is key.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean 事前, used before nouns like 녹화 (recording)

examples.text: 사전 녹화 좀 떠주면 안 되냐?
examples.trans: Couldn't you pre-record them for us?
Advance preparation is needed.

examples.text: 우리 공과 사는 구분하죠. 이건 공적인 스케줄이니까 사적인 대화는 삼가는 게 좋겠다는 얘기예요.

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Often used directly without a locative particle to mean 'here'.

examples.trans: Please sit here.
Here is our office.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.
What day of the week is it today?

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.

meanings.en: older male friend or colleague (used by a female)

examples.trans: I have one older brother.

Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.

examples.text: 이번에 출연자들 각자 절친들 집에 초대하는 거, 신디 팔로잉을 승찬이 보내볼까?

examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 사고라는 건 하필이 세 번이면 일어난다.
examples.trans: An accident happens whenever three bad coincidences line up in a row.
Here the word for 'unlucky timing' is key.

meanings.note: Compound of 하다 (to do) and 주다 (to give).

examples.trans: Please help me (do helping for me).
Please do this for me.

examples.text: 뭐야, 사전 허락도 없이? 왜 미리 말을 안 해줘, 지금 메이크업도 제대로 안 했는데!
